extracted.intended_audience: general public, potential victims, media, and other stakeholders in the Theranos prosecutions
extracted.subtask_description: A U.S. Attorney's Office news/case-information page summarizing indictment allegations, charges, sentencing, victim-submission instructions, court access notices, and contact information for a federal criminal prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged fraud against doctors and patients
rubrics_metrics.description: The indictment alleges Holmes and Balwani used advertisements and solicitations to encourage and induce doctors and patients to use Theranos’s blood testing laboratory services, even though the defendants knew Theranos was not capable of consistently producing accurate and reliable results for certain blood tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As alleged: defendants defrauded doctors and patients (1) by making false claims concerning Theranos’s ability to provide accurate, fast, reliable, and cheap blood tests and test results, and (2) by omitting information concerning the limits of and problems with Theranos’s technologies. The indictment lists specific tests (calcium, chloride, potassium, bicarbonate, HIV, Hba1C, hCG, and sodium) and alleges the tests performed on Theranos technology were likely to contain inaccurate and unreliable results. The defendants used interstate electronic wires to purchase advertisements intended to induce individuals to purchase Theranos blood tests at Walgreens stores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged fraud against investors
rubrics_metrics.description: The indictment alleges defendants made numerous misrepresentations to potential investors about Theranos’s financial condition and future prospects and about the technology underlying Theranos’s testing services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific alleged misrepresentations include claims that Theranos conducted tests using Theranos-manufactured analyzers when it used third-party commercially available analyzers, and revenue projections (e.g., over $100 million in revenues and break-even in 2014; approximately $1 billion in revenues in 2015) that defendants knew were materially false or overstated. The indictment alleges use of direct communications, marketing materials, statements to the media, financial statements, models, and other information to defraud potential investors, and false claims about the capabilities of the analyzer (TSPU/Edison/minilab).

rubrics_metrics.name: Means and methods alleged (use of wires and promotional materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: The indictment alleges use of interstate electronic wires, advertisements, solicitations, direct communications, marketing materials, media statements, financial statements, and models to induce purchase of tests and investments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: defendants used interstate electronic wires to purchase advertisements and represented tests were cheaper than conventional labs to induce purchases at Walgreens stores; used a combination of communications and materials to defraud investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal counts charged
rubrics_metrics.description: The indictment charges each defendant with two counts of conspiracy to commit wire fraud in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1349, and nine counts of wire fraud in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1343.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the statutory bases for federal prosecution as stated on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged falsity and omissions regarding technology capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants allegedly represented that Theranos developed a revolutionary/proprietary analyzer able to perform a full range of clinical tests from a finger stick, producing more accurate and reliable results at faster speeds; but allegedly knew many of these representations were false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged problems: analyzer had accuracy and reliability problems, performed a limited number of tests, was slower than some competing devices, and in some respects could not compete with existing conventional machines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentencing outcomes and post-conviction procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences, supervision, surrender dates, and restitution hearings described for both defendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: Balwani sentenced to 155 months (12 years, 11 months) with three years supervised release; Holmes sentenced to 135 months (11 years, 3 months) with three years supervised release. Parties instructed to meet and agree on a future restitution hearing date; no fine assessed for Holmes. Surrender dates (Balwani ordered to surrender March 15, 2023; Holmes ordered to surrender April 27, 2023). A hearing to determine restitution amount will be scheduled in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice regarding court dates and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Public notice that due to high interest in the case, there is a separate webpage for news and information about access to proceedings and case information, and that dates are subject to change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: check the Judge’s calendar before attending because dates are subject to change on short notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions and requirements for potential victims submitting information
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Attorney’s Office and investigating agencies are seeking information from those who may be victims; if you believe you are a patient victim, you must fill out a questionnaire and submit by a specified deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: complete and submit the questionnaire no later than September 6, 2022; email submissions to oci.theranos@fda.hhs.gov with subject line 'US v Holmes & Balwani'. The office is unable to accept late submissions. All responses are voluntary, but complete submissions are useful for identifying respondents as potential victims and supplying the Court with information necessary for sentencing. Respondents may be contacted by law enforcement for additional information. The U.S. Attorney’s Office cannot act as your attorney or provide legal advice; victims may seek counsel independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and contact information for assistance and press inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Phone numbers and email addresses for the Mega Victim Case Assistance Program and the Public Information Officer provided for case assistance and press inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For case assistance: (844) 527-5299 or USAO.MCAP@USDOJ.GOV. For press inquiries: Public Information Officer at 415-436-7264 or email Abraham.Simmons@usdoj.gov.
